title: 06 — Excel: Read and Write
html:
06 — Excel: Read and Write

The one idea: Excel is a delivery format, not a storage format. Do the work in Polars and Parquet, then write a well-formatted workbook at the end with write_excel. Read incoming Excel with the fast calamine engine and declare the types you expect.

1. What it is

Task Tool Notes
Read .xlsx/.xls/.ods pl.read_excel with engine="calamine" (default, via fastexcel) By far the fastest. Reads to Arrow without copying
Read tricky files engine="openpyxl" or "xlsx2csv" Slower, more tolerant
Write a new workbook df.write_excel (uses xlsxwriter) Tables, formats, formulas, totals, conditional formats, sparklines
Several sheets in one file Open xlsxwriter.Workbook(...) and pass it to each write_excel
Edit an existing workbook (templates) openpyxl See 07

write_excel options worth knowing:

Option What it does
worksheet, position Sheet name, and the top-left cell ("B2")
table_style, table_name Writes an Excel table (filters, banding, structured references)
column_formats, dtype_formats Number formats per column, or per type (all dates, all floats)
column_totals, row_totals Total row and column, as live Excel formulas
formulas New columns calculated by Excel, e.g. "=[@amount]/SUM([amount])"
conditional_formats Data bars, colour scales, icon sets, rules
autofit, column_widths, freeze_panes, hide_gridlines Layout

2. Why it matters

  • Finance, operations and clients live in Excel. A report that opens formatted and correct saves hours of manual work.
  • Excel is slow to read and write and loses types. Keep the pipeline in Parquet and only touch Excel at the edges.
  • An Excel row limit of 1,048,576 means large extracts don't fit. Summarise, or split across sheets.

3. The main ideas

3.1 Write tables, not cell dumps

Write data as an Excel table (table_style/table_name). Users get filters and banding, and formulas can use structured references such as Trades[amount] that grow with the data.

3.2 Let Excel calculate what users will change

Totals and shares written as formulas stay right when someone edits a value. Values computed in Polars are fixed numbers. Choose per column.

3.3 Read with declared types

read_excel infers types from the first rows (infer_schema_length=100). Use schema_overrides for IDs, codes with leading zeros, and decimals, and columns= to read only what you need. sheet_id=0 reads every sheet into a dict.

4. Working code

The script writes a summary sheet (formats, totals, data bars, a live share formula) and a 50,000-row detail table into one workbook, reads it back, and checks the round trip.

import time
import openpyxl
import polars as pl
from xlsxwriter import Workbook

trades = pl.read_parquet("data/trades.parquet")
summary = (
    trades.group_by("category")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("trades"), pl.col("amount").sum().alias("amount"),
         pl.col("amount").mean().alias("avg_amount"))
    .sort("amount", descending=True)
    .with_columns(pl.col("category").cast(pl.String))
)
detail = trades.head(50_000).with_columns(pl.col("side", "category").cast(pl.String))

# Several sheets in one workbook: open an xlsxwriter Workbook and pass it to each write_excel call.
t = time.perf_counter()
with Workbook("data/report.xlsx") as wb:
    summary.write_excel(
        wb, worksheet="Summary", position="B2", table_style="Table Style Medium 2",
        column_formats={"amount": "#,##0", "avg_amount": "#,##0.00", "trades": "#,##0", "share": "0.0%"},
        column_totals={"trades": "sum", "amount": "sum"},
        conditional_formats={"amount": "data_bar"},
        formulas={"share": "=[@amount]/SUM([amount])"},
        autofit=True,
    )
    detail.write_excel(
        wb, worksheet="Detail", table_name="Trades",
        dtype_formats={pl.Date: "dd-mmm-yyyy", pl.Float64: "#,##0.00"},
        freeze_panes="A2", autofit=True,
    )
print(f"wrote 2 sheets ({detail.height:,} detail rows) in {time.perf_counter() - t:.2f} s")

# Read back with the default calamine engine (fastexcel). sheet_id=0 returns every sheet.
t = time.perf_counter()
sheets = pl.read_excel("data/report.xlsx", sheet_id=0)
print(f"read {list(sheets)} in {time.perf_counter() - t:.2f} s")
back = pl.read_excel("data/report.xlsx", sheet_name="Detail",
                     schema_overrides={"trade_id": pl.Int64, "fund_id": pl.Int64})
print(back.schema)
print("detail round-trip equal:", back.select(detail.columns).equals(detail))

# Formulas are stored for Excel to calculate; a reader sees the formula text, not a number.
ws = openpyxl.load_workbook("data/report.xlsx")["Summary"]
print("C3:", ws["C3"].value, "| formula cell F3:", ws["F3"].value, "| number format D3:", ws["D3"].number_format)

Output:

wrote 2 sheets (50,000 detail rows) in 1.91 s
read ['Summary', 'Detail'] in 0.13 s
Schema({'trade_id': Int64, 'fund_id': Int64, 'amount': Float64, 'side': String, 'trade_date': Date, 'category': String})
detail round-trip equal: True
C3: 199895 | formula cell F3: =[[#This Row],amount]/SUM([amount]) | number format D3: #,##0

What to notice:

  • Reading was over 10× faster than writing (0.13 s against 1.91 s). Writing styled workbooks costs time, so keep detail sheets to what people will use.
  • The detail sheet round-tripped exactly once the schema was declared, dates included.
  • The share column holds a formula, rewritten by XlsxWriter into Excel's full structured-reference form. Excel calculates it on open. A Python reader sees the formula text, not a number.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Using Excel as an intermediate format between pipeline steps.
  2. Writing more than about a million rows to one sheet.
  3. Leaving types to inference on read, so IDs lose leading zeros and become numbers.
  4. Hard-coded totals that go stale when users edit cells.
  5. Writing Categorical/Enum columns without casting to String first, if a downstream tool expects plain text.

6. Exercise (1 hour)

  1. Add a sparkline column of monthly amounts per category to the summary (sparklines=).
  2. Add a colour-scale conditional format to avg_amount, and freeze the header row of the summary.
  3. Read only trade_id and amount from the detail sheet with columns=, and time it against reading everything.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Which engine does read_excel use by default, and why?
  2. How do you write several sheets into one workbook?
  3. When should a column be an Excel formula rather than a value?
  4. Why declare schema_overrides when reading Excel?
  5. What can't write_excel do that a template workflow needs?

Answers

  1. calamine (through fastexcel). It is the fastest and reads straight into Arrow.
  2. Open an xlsxwriter.Workbook and pass it to each write_excel call with a different worksheet.
  3. When users will change inputs and expect totals or ratios to follow.
  4. Inference can turn IDs, codes and decimals into the wrong types.
  5. Edit an existing workbook. XlsxWriter only creates new files, so templates need openpyxl.
